t: #3576 Transform Array to All Equal Elements
o: We may flip adjacent pairs at most k times and want all elements equal. Flipping at index i toggles a shared factor between neighbors, so a left-to-right greedy is forced: scanning i = 0..n-2, if the effective value at i does not match the target we must flip at i. Whether the last element can match determines feasibility. Try both targets (all 1s and all -1s) and check whether either needs at most k operations. n up to 1e5 means an O(n) simulation is required.
k: A greedy left-to-right pass is optimal: each flip decision at i is forced by whether position i currently matches the target.
Feasibility for a target is determined by whether the last element ends up matching after the greedy pass.
Try both targets and compare minimum operations against k.

a.n: Approach 1: Greedy simulation for both targets
a.i: Simulate the forced greedy for target 1 and target -1. Keep a flag f = whether we flipped at the previous index; the effective value at i is nums[i] * (-1)^f. If it mismatches, flip at i (increment ops, toggle f). At the end verify the last element; otherwise the target is infeasible.
s: Define ops(target): scan i from 0 to n-2 maintaining flip flag f.
If nums[i] * sign(f) != target, increment ops and toggle f.
After the loop check nums[n-1] * sign(f) == target; if not, return infinity.

w: The greedy is exchange-argument optimal: delaying a needed flip never helps. Pitfall: forgetting to validate the last element (it cannot be fixed by a flip at n-1), and n = 1 (always true). Follow-up: return the minimum number of operations instead of a boolean.
